description:
Submit a physical-world requirement (a part, product, device, or capability that must exist in the physical world). a2a2p resolves it and returns a RESOLUTION REPORT: a recommended path (best existing commercial solution vs. custom fabrication), pricing, tradeoffs, a delivery plan with contingencies and expedite options, and a business case when business context is provided. Response is asynchronous: you receive a request_id immediately with an instant spec_review. Poll check_request_status; as soon as an automated draft exists it is returned with an a2a2p.resolution-report-delivery receipt that distinguishes machine_draft from operator_published. If the finite attempt budget is exhausted, status returns generation_failed; if the bounded automatic retry window expires first, it returns generation_expired. Either terminal state permits only a new caller-confirmed request from caller-held input. Operator review and publication are not guaranteed or subject to a service-level promise. No state is professional engineering certification or a supplier quote.

ENTRY MODES — arrive with what you have:
  • fully_specified: provide 'specification' (part_type, material, process, dimensions, tolerance_class, design_files). Go straight to resolution report.
  • intent_only: provide 'intent' (purpose, environment, functional_requirements, quantity, timeline, priority). a2a2p recommends 2-3 specification options with tradeoffs.
  • partial: provide what you know in either layer; a2a2p fills the gaps.

Layer 1 (intent) describes the PROBLEM. Layer 2 (specification) describes the SOLUTION. At minimum, provide 'requirement' (legacy) or 'intent.purpose' (structured) — one line describing what you need. Use 'rejected_alternatives' to record options already ruled out.

budget_usd.description: Approximate budget in USD. Maps to intent.budget_envelope.

business_context.description: Optional business requirements (expected volumes, cost targets, ROI constraints). If provided, the quote includes a business case.

callback_url.description: Optional HTTPS URL. When the quote is ready, a2a2p POSTs it as JSON to this URL.

constraints.description: Hard constraints: tolerances, certifications, materials to avoid, size/weight limits. Maps to intent.functional_requirements.

contact.description: Optional email or callback endpoint for quote delivery.

deadline.description: Required delivery date or timeframe. Maps to intent.timeline.

intent.description: Layer 1 — the problem. What the physical matter needs to DO. Use this for intent-driven requests where the agent describes purpose and a2a2p recommends solutions.

alternates_acceptable.description: Whether a supplier may propose a different material, process or stock size.

load_case.description: Optional bounded structural sanity check. State an explicit static point-load model and rectangular section; height_mm is the bending direction.

allowable_shear_stress_mpa.description: Optional requester-supplied transverse-shear design allowable; evaluated independently and never inferred from handbook data.

allowable_stress_mpa.description: Optional requester-supplied design allowable; never inferred from handbook yield.

elastic_modulus_gpa.description: Optional requester-supplied Young's modulus. Otherwise the matched material handbook reference is used and labeled.

minimum_factor_of_safety.description: Optional acceptance criterion; evaluated only with requester-supplied yield_strength_mpa.

model.description: Supported deterministic models: cantilever_end_load or simply_supported_center_load. Other values are preserved but reported as unsupported.

height_mm.description: Rectangular section depth in the bending direction, millimetres.

yield_strength_mpa.description: Optional exact grade/condition/product-form datasheet value supplied by the requester.

max_load.description: Maximum load magnitude. A Newton scalar is preferred; { value, unit: "N" } remains accepted.

max_weight.description: Maximum weight of the part in kg.

geometric_envelope.description: Max bounding box in mm if known.

inspection_documents.description: Inspection or material documents required with the parts, or "none required".

priority.description: What matters most when tradeoffs arise.

purpose.description: What the physical matter needs to accomplish (one non-whitespace line minimum, required).

quote_by.description: Date a quote is needed by.

ship_to_region.description: Delivery region. When present, a supplier package asks for a price including freight to it; when absent, freight is excluded.

quantity.description: Number of units needed. Maps to intent.quantity.

rejected_alternatives.description: Options already considered and ruled out. Prevents re-suggesting and builds the learning corpus.

field.description: Which spec field (material, process, part_type, etc.).

requirement.description: Plain-language description of the physical need. Maps to intent.purpose. Include function, dimensions, materials, load/performance requirements, environment, and interfaces where known.

specification.description: Layer 2 — the solution. What the physical matter IS. Populate what is known. Precise specifications produce faster, tighter quotes. Controlled vocabularies are preferred but open values are accepted.

cutting.description: Cutting-tool constraints for routed or milled profiles.

inside_corner_relief.description: dogbone or t_bone: the supplier adds that relief; in_file: relief is already drawn; not_required: tool-radius corners are acceptable.

tool_diameter_mm.description: Smallest cutter that will be used. Inside corners and holes with a smaller radius are flagged against the measured DXF.

design_files.description: Temporary or externally hosted manufacturing file references ({url, format, optional role}). Accepted upload aliases: stl, step, stp, dxf, pdf; shared downstream ceiling: 8388608 bytes.

dimensions.description: Critical dimensions with units, or bounding box.

material.description: Material (controlled vocab preferred: aluminum_6061, steel_304, PLA, ...; open values accepted).

notes.description: Manufacturing notes for the supplier. Carried verbatim into the supplier package; never parsed into facts. State anything a check must use in its structured field.

sheet_stock.description: The sheet a flat part is cut from. For plywood a supplier needs face_grade, nominal and actual thickness, ply_count and glue_class; for MDF, grade and thickness. Missing facts are asked, never chosen by a2a2p.

actual_thickness_mm.description: Measured or specified actual thickness. Stock-relative tolerances also satisfy this: the joint follows the sheet.

face_grade.description: Face/back veneer grade, for example B/BB.

glue_class.description: Bond class, for example EN 314-2 class 1 (interior) or class 3 (exterior).

grade.description: Panel grade for MDF and similar boards, for example standard or moisture_resistant.

grain_direction.description: Face-grain direction relative to the declared X/Y dimensions.

tolerance_class.description: Required precision: coarse, medium, fine, precision.

allowance_mm.description: Added to the measured stock thickness; negative for an interference fit.

fit_class.description: Optional label such as push_fit or press_fit.

tolerances.description: Exact numeric tolerance callouts keyed by feature. They govern over tolerance_class for the named feature. Forms: a positive number (plus or minus that amount); { nominal, plus, minus }; or a stock-relative rule { relative_to: "measured_stock_thickness", allowance_mm, plus, minus, fit_class } for joints cut to the sheet actually used.

name: request_physical_solution
